questions.question: Ellora Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, are located in which of the following hills?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charanadri Hills.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Ellora Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, are located in Charanadri Hills, Aurangabad district of Maharastra.
 
• There are **over 100 caves **at the site, all excavated from the basalt cliffs in the Charanandri Hills, **34 of which are open to the public.**
 
• It is **one of the largest rock-cut Hindu temple cave complexes in the world,** with artwork dating from the period 600–1000 CE.
 
• **Cave 16** features **the largest single monolithic rock excavation in the world, the Kailash temple,** a chariot-shaped monument **dedicated to the god Shiva. **
 
• All of the Ellora monuments were** built during the Rashtrakuta dynasty.**
 
• These consist of 17 Hindu, 12 Buddhist, and 5 Jain caves.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a percussion instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Sarod.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sarod** is not a percussion instrument whereas Mridangam, Tabla, and Ghatam are **percussion instruments**.
 
• In percussion, the sound is produced by striking the animal skin which has been stretched across an earthen or metal pot or a wooden barrel or frame.
 
• The main categories are-
 
 
• Oordhwaka,
 
• Ankya,
 
• Alingya, and
 
• the waisted or the Damaru family of drums
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tabla** pair is a set of two vertical Oordhwaka drums.
 
• **Ankya drums** are held horizontally before the musician and usually, both sides are covered with animal hide.
 
• **Oordhwaka drums** are placed vertically before the musician and sound is produced by striking them with sticks or fingers.
 
• **Alingya drums** have the animal hide fixed to a wooden round frame and are embraced or held close to the body with one hand while the other hand is used for playing the instrument.
 
• **Damru family** is also known as the hourglass variety of drums as their shape resembles an hourglass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea9dab231bacb90443f7815bbd6e9af2762117c9714ed485d416439aba22297e.png]

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is observed by the tribal people of Jharkhand?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Bhagta Parab.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• This jubilee comes between the period of spring and summer.
 
• Among the ethnical people of Jharkhand, Bhagta Parab is best known as the deification of Budha Baba.
 
• People gormandize during the day and carry the bathing Pahan the clerk, to the ethnical mandir called Sarana Mandir.
 
• The Pahan occasionally called Laya, gets out of the pond, the addicts make a chain, locking their shanks with each other, and come forward to offer their bare casket to Laya for a walkover.
 
• After deification in the evening, addicts take part in dynamic and vigorous Chhau cotillion with lots of gymnastic conduct and masks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nongkrem**:

 
 
• The Nongkrem dance festival is celebrated during Autumn at Smit, the cultural center of the Khasi Hills.
 
• A five-day-long religious festival of the Khasis, Ka Pomblang Nongkrem dance is popularly known as the Nongkrem dance.
 
 
 
• **Losar:**
 
 
• The Tibetan word “ Losar ”, which translates to “ New Year ” in English is the most popular and significant jubilee of the North East Indian state of Sikkim and is celebrated with great enthusiasm every time.
 
• The history of the Losar festival predates the arrival of Buddhism in Tibet and its neighboring regions like parts of India, Bhutan, and Nepal.
 
 
 
• **Suata**:
 
 
• Like the Ghadalya festival of Malwa, the Suata festival is famous in the Bundelkhand region.
 
• In this festival an ornate statue of the demon is installed on the wall and in the upper part of it, a statue of ShivaParvati is placed, the sun and moon are made on the wall, then the young women worship and sing.

questions.question: As per the Natya Shastra, idiophones are called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghana Vadya.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Ghana Vadya or Idiophones/Solid instruments which do not require tuning- 
 
• The earliest instruments invented by man are said to be the Ghana Vadya.
 
• Once constructed, this variety of instrument do not need special tuning prior to playing.
 
• They are principally rhythmic in function and are best suited as accompaniment to folk and tribal music and dance.
 
• E.g - Jal Tarang, Ghatam etc

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Instruments have been listed below. 
 
• Avanaddha Vadya or Membranophones/Percussion instruments -
 
 
• In the Avanaddha Vadya category of instruments, the sound is produced by striking the animal skin which has been stretched across an earthern or metal pot or a wooden barrel or frame.
 
• E.g - Tabla, Mridangam, Nagara, Damaru etc. 
 
 
 
• Sushira Vadya or Aerophones/Wind instruments -
 
 
• In the Sushira Vadya group, the sound is produced by blowing air into a hollow column.
 
• The pitch of the note is determined by controlling the air passage and the melody is played by using the fingers to open and close the instrument.
 
• E.g - Flutes, Shehnai, Nadaswaram, etc. 
 
 
 
• Tata Vadya or Chordophones/Stringed instruments - 
 
 
• ​The tata vadya is a category of instruments in which sound is produced by the vibration of a string or chord.
 
• These vibrations are caused by plucking or by bowing on the string which has been pulled taut.
 
• E.g - Veena, Sitar, Sarangi etc.

questions.question: As of March 2022, which of the following dance forms has NOT been listed as a classical dance in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer __**Lavani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Classical dance

 
 
• Classical dances are performed by professional or highly trained dancers who have studied their form for many years.
 
• There are nine classical Dances in India.
 
• Classical dance expresses a story or theme and this form of art lies in the religious Hindu music theatre styles. It represents the culture.
 
• They are
 
 
• Kathak from North India,
 
• Sattriya of Assam,
 
• Bharatnatyam of Tamil Nadu,
 
• Kuchipudi of Andhra Pradesh,
 
• Kathakali and Mohiniaattam of Kerala,
 
• Manipuri of Northeast India, and
 
• Odissi of Odisha.
 
• **Chhau Eastern India**
 
 
 
• It is the right way to connect with your feelings, coordinate and move the movement skills and build strength and stability in your body.
 
• Lavani is not a classical dance of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** __Lavani**__

 
• Lavani is a popular music genre in Maharashtra, India.
 
• It is a traditional song that is done to the rhythms of the Dholki, a percussion instrument.
 
• It is known for its strong beat.
 
• It has made significant contributions to the growth of Marathi folk theatre.
 
• It is done by female artists in Maharashtra and southern Madhya Pradesh who wear nine-yard-long sarees.
 
• The songs are sung at a fast pace.
 
• Lavani dance evolved in Maharashtra during the 18th and 19th centuries.
 
• This dance genre was prominent under the Peshawari Dynasty, which was based in Pune.
 
• It was traditionally done by Dhangars or shepherds from Solapur, Maharashtra.
 
• The major theme of the Lavani is the numerous types of love between man and woman. 
 
• The Lavani's various topics include the love between husband and wife, soldier's amorous escapades, the woman's farewell to the husband who is about to join the war, and the anguish of separation.

questions.question:
Which of the following pair of Thumri singing - characteristic is correct?

I. Poorab - fairly slow and staid

II. Punjab - more mercurial
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ​An** Indian musical style **known as** thumri features vocals.**
 
• The Hindi verb **thumuknaa**, which means **"to walk with a dance gait,**" is the root of the word **"thumri."**
 
• The art form has ties to **dance, dramatic movements, light erotica, evocative love poems, and folk music.**
 
• It is especially famous in **Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• It has a** romantic or spiritual tone.**
 
• **Awadhi and Brij Bhasha,** two Hindi dialects from Uttar Pradesh, are typically used for the **lyrics.**
 
• There are** two styles** of Thumri singing:
 
 
• **the Poorab or Banaras** which is fairly **slow and staid** and
 
• the **Punjab style** which is more** mercurial.**

questions.question: ‘Kalbelia’ is a folk-dance of which of the following states of India?

questions.question: ‘Sangita Ratnakara’ by Pandit Sarngadeva is a _______ Century treatise on Indian classical music.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13th.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The** Sangita-Ratnakara **is **Sanskrit **for **"Ocean of Music and Dance."**
 
• It is one of the most significant Indian** texts on musicology.**
 
• In the** thirteenth centur**y, **Sarngadeva **wrote it in** Sanskrit.**
 
• The author served in **King Singhana II's court **during the **Yadava dynasty**, whose seat of government was in** Devagiri, Maharashtra**.
 
• There are** seven chapters** in the text.
 
• **Svaragatadhyaya, Ragavivekadhyaya, Prakirnakadhyaya, Prabandhadhyaya, Taladhyaya, and Vadyadhyaya,** the first six chapters, cover a variety o**f musical topics and instruments.**
 
• **Nartanadhyaya's** final chapter discusses **dance.**

questions.question: Thaipusam festival is celebrated in which of the following Indian states?

questions.question: Which festival is celebrated in the month of February by the Angami tribe of Nagaland?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Sekrenyi festival.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sekrenyi is celebrated annually as part of the **Mini Hornbill Tribal Festival in the month of February.**
 
• The Sekrenyi festival is the biggest festival of the Angami lineage and it falls on the 25th day of the Angami month of Kezei.
 
• It's a festivity of sanctification accompanied by feasting and singing.
 
• Locally known as** Phousanyi,** Sekrenyi of Nagaland is essentially a festival of the Angami Nagas. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Losoong Festival:**

 
 
• Losoong Festival is the Sikkimese New Year, of the Bhutia tribe, celebrated every time in the month of December.
 
• This tribe is veritably notorious in eastern India.
 
• Cham dances are performed by Buddhist Monks.
 
 
 
• **Hornbill festival:**
 
 
• The Hornbill Festival, which is called the ‘Festivals of Festivals’, is a 10-day annual cultural fest of Nagaland that showcases the rich and diverse Naga ethnicity through folk dances, traditional music, local cuisine, handicraft, art workshops, etc.
 
 
 
• **Majuli festival:**
 
 
• It is celebrated in the northeast side of the country, in the state of Assam.
 
• The place to celebrate the jubilee is the bank of River Luit, which happens to have the biggest swash islet in the world.
 
• This jubilee starts on the 21st of November each time and continues to the 24th of the same month.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first woman to learn the all-male style of Kathakali and was also the founder of Darpana Academy Of Performing Arts that caters to various performing arts like dance, music, drama and puppetry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mrinalini Sarabhai.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mrinalini Sarabhai**** **was the first woman to learn the all-male style of **Kathakali **and was also the founder of **Darpana Academy Of Performing Arts** that caters to various performing arts like dance, music, drama and puppetry.
 
• Mrinalini Sarabhai was an Indian classical dancer and choreographer.
 
• She married to the famous scientist Vikram Sarabhai.
 
• Mrinalini Sarabhai was a recipient of the Padma Shri (1965) as well as the Padma Bhushan (1992).
 
• She was also awarded the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in New Delhi in the year 1994.
 
• Her biggest contribution to the field of dance remains the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts, which she established with her husband in Ahmedabad, in 1949.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Niveditha Arjun** is an Indian actress, producer and dancer.

• **Ustad Bundu Khan (1880 – 1955)**:​

 
 
• He was a **sarangi playe**r from India.
 
• Bundu Khan was also a** musicologist or musical theorist**.
 
• In** June 1934**, his music book **Jauhar-i-Mausiqi in Urdu** was concurrently released in **Hindi and Urdu.**
 
• In **1985**, the President of Pakistan presented him with the** Pride of Performance Award.**
 
 
 
• **Santosh Mishra**:
 
 
• He was one of Varanasi's most successful sarangi players.
 
• He is the **eldest son of Pandit Bhagwan Das Mishra** who was a veteran of the **Banaras Gharana.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sitar:**

 
 
• A **plucked stringed instrument** with** moveable frets **and a **gourd resonator** is known as a sitar.
 
 
 
• **shehnai:**
 
 
• It is composed of wood, with a **double reed** on one end, and a** flared bell **made of **wood or metal **on the other.
 
 
 
• **sarangi:**
 
 
• A short-necked **bowed string instrument** is the sarangi.
 
 
 
• **sarod:**
 
 
• A** stringed instrument** known as the sarod is utilized in** Hindustani music** on the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals of Punjab is traditionally associated with the harvest of rabi crops?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Baisakhi.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Baisakhi** festivals of Punjab is traditionally associated with the harvest of** rabi crops.**

 
• **Wheat crops** could be seen growing and swinging all across Punjab at this time of year.
 
• Sikhs hold kirtans, visit local Gurdwaras, and community fairs, hold Nagar kirtan processions, raise the Nishan Sahib flag, and gather to socialize and share festive foods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• According to the Khalsa sambat, the Khalsa calendar starts with the creation of the Khalsa which is 1 Vaisakh 1756 Bikrami (13 April 1699).
 
• Vaisakhi has been the traditional Sikh New Year.
 
• The alternative Nanakshahi calendar begins its year a month earlier on 1 Chait which generally falls on 14 March and begins with the birth year of the Guru Nanak Dev in 1469.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hola Mohalla,** also called Hola, is a three-day long Sikh festival which normally falls in March.
 
• **Maghi **is the regional name of the Hindu festival of Makar Sankranti celebrated in Punjab and Himachal Pradesh.
 
• **The Muktsar fair **is one of the largest Sikh fairs held in Muktsar Sahib commonly referred to as Muktsar.
